newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bond issuers seen heading for more defaults.
newsitem.headline: Thai bond issuers seen heading for more defaults.

text.p: Bond market analysts warned on Wednesday that more Thai issuers of domestic debt paper and Euro-convertible debentures may default on their payments.

Teera Phutrakul, managing director of Thai Capital Management Co Ltd, said a default by One Holding Plc on bills of exchange worth $13.5 million in March was just the tip of the iceberg on woes faced by Thailand's ailing financial sector.
"I think the default by One Holding, whose papers were among the 10 most actively traded in mid-1996...is just the tip of the iceberg," he told a bond market seminar.

Ismail Dalla, president of Washington Assets Management Inc, said the bond market was watching with concern whether some Thai issuers of Euro-convertible debentures could meet debt repayment obligations when a lot of their paper matures in 1998.
"The concern stems from the fact that many of these bonds are currently trading at very high yields," he said.
Dalla said most cash-strapped Thai companies were in the troubled property sector.
Housing developer Somprasong Land Plc in February failed to honour a $3.1 million debt due on its $80 million Euro-convertible issue.
The property industry is reeling under a four-year slump and its growing non-performing assets have shaken creditor banks and finance companies and depressed the stock market this year.
But Emil Nguy, managing director of Income Partners Asset Management, struck a more optimistic note saying his fund management firm would continue investing in Thailand.
Nguy described Thailand's sharply slowing economy and weak exports as short-term setbacks judging from its high-growth track record in the past decade.

"I see Thailand's recent downgrade (by Moody's Investors Service Inc) as just a blip of its irreversible long-term growth trend...unless there is something in the closet that we don't know," he told the same function.

Income Partners, founded in 1993, manages investment funds worth more than $1 billion, including five open-ended funds with money invested in fixed income and money market instruments in 10 Asian countries.
Nguy said the firm put 15-25 percent of its investment in Asian countries in Thailand.
"We're an investor in Thailand and will continue to be," he said.
